<objective>
Replace `PenetrationModalComponent`'s timer-gated, one-shot state fetch with a signal input feeding a `takeUntil` + `distinctUntilChanged` RxJS lifecycle, and make the state service the component's single source of panel state (D-10, D-11, D-12, D-13).

Purpose: RACE-01. Today `ngOnChanges` schedules a 300ms timer, inside which it subscribes to the state service and immediately unsubscribes — a one-shot read whose correctness depends on 300ms being "long enough" for overlays to have landed. The component simultaneously accepts `leftPanelState`/`rightPanelState` `@Input`s from an async pipe that its own code comment describes as possibly stale, then picks between the two sources with a `??` fallback. Both mechanisms go away.

Named, deliberate behavior deltas (this is the one phase permitted to change behavior; each delta is enumerable at review time):
1. D-10 — modal content becomes visible immediately rather than after 300ms, so it now fades/slides in together with the modal shell instead of popping in after the shell settles.
2. D-11 — the modal follows state changes made while it is open, instead of freezing at open-time state.

Output: signal-input-driven reactive modal, `app.component.html` binding trimmed, spec expanded.
</objective>

  <behavior>
    - Setting the `isOpen` input to `true` makes `showContent` true synchronously within the same change-detection turn (no timer, no `tick(300)` needed in a spec).
    - While `isOpen` is true, pushing a new state through the state service updates the component's internal left/right panel state and re-runs position calculation.
    - Setting `isOpen` back to `false` sets `showContent` false and clears the internal left/right panel state, and further state-service emissions no longer reach the component.
    - Destroying the component while open stops all further state-service-driven work.
    - Two consecutive state emissions whose left/right panel model id, scale, overlay id list, overlay scales, and overlay rotations are all equal do not re-run position calculation twice.
  </behavior>
  <action>
Rework `PenetrationModalComponent`'s lifecycle.

<!-- planner-discipline-allow: setTimeout -->
<!-- planner-discipline-allow: ngOnChanges -->

Input surface (D-12, D-13):
- Change `isOpen` from an `@Input()` boolean to a signal input: `isOpen = input(false);` importing
  `input` from `@angular/core`. Parent binding syntax `[isOpen]="showPenetrationModal"` is unchanged.
- Delete the `@Input() leftPanelState` and `@Input() rightPanelState` fields entirely.
- Keep `@Output() close = new EventEmitter<void>()` as-is. Do NOT migrate any other member to signals —
  D-13 explicitly scopes the signal migration to `isOpen` only, and rejects converting `showContent`,
  the transforms, or the dimension fields.

Lifecycle (D-10, D-11):
- Delete the entire `ngOnChanges` method and drop `OnChanges` from the class's `implements` clause and
  from the `@angular/core` import list. There must be no `setTimeout` anywhere in this file when the
  task is done — ROADMAP Success Criterion 1 asserts its absence.
- Add `private destroy$ = new Subject<void>();` and, in `ngOnDestroy`, call `this.destroy$.next()` then
  `this.destroy$.complete()` (mirroring `compare-modal.component.ts`'s teardown).
- In the CONSTRUCTOR body (not `ngOnInit` — `toObservable` requires an Angular injection context and
  throws NG0203 outside it, per RESEARCH.md Pitfall 1), build the chain:
  `toObservable(this.isOpen)` (imported from `@angular/core/rxjs-interop`) piped through
  `switchMap(open => ...)` then `takeUntil(this.destroy$)`, and subscribe.
  - When `open` is false: set `this.showContent = false`, set `this.leftPanelStateInternal = null` and
    `this.rightPanelStateInternal = null`, and return `EMPTY` (imported from `rxjs`). This reproduces
    today's close branch and is what tears the inner state subscription down on close.
  - When `open` is true: set `this.showContent = true` immediately (D-10 — no deferral), then return
    `this.stateManagementService.state.pipe(distinctUntilChanged((a, b) => this.panelStateEqual(a, b)))`.
    Put `distinctUntilChanged` on the INNER observable, not after `switchMap`, so the dedupe window
    resets each time the modal reopens rather than suppressing the first emission of a new session.
  - In the `subscribe` callback: assign `this.leftPanelStateInternal = state.leftPanel`,
    `this.rightPanelStateInternal = state.rightPanel`, then call `this.initializePenetrator()` and
    `this.calculatePositions()` — the same three actions the timer callback performs today, in the same order.
- Add `private panelStateEqual(a: AppState, b: AppState): boolean` comparing only the fields this modal
  reads, modeled on `ModelAttachmentDefaultsService.panelDataEqual`: for each of `leftPanel` and
  `rightPanel`, compare `selectedModel?.id`, `scale`, the sorted joined overlay id list, and — for each
  overlay id — the entry in `overlayScales` and in `overlayRotations`. Return false as soon as any differ.
  A default `===` comparator is useless here because this codebase creates a new state object on every
  update (RESEARCH.md Pitfall 2).
- Move the measurement-unit subscription out of the deleted lifecycle hook: in the same constructor,
  subscribe to `this.stateManagementService.globalSettings$` piped through `takeUntil(this.destroy$)`,
  assigning `this.currentUnit = settings.measurementUnit`. Delete the `unitSubscription` field and its
  manual `unsubscribe()` in `ngOnDestroy`.

Single source of panel state (D-12):
- Delete `getEffectiveLeftState()` and `getEffectiveRightState()`.
- Update all five consumers to read the internal fields directly: `initializePenetrator`,
  `canBePenetrator`, `canBeReceiver`, `getPenetratorState`, and `getReceiverState` now use
  `this.leftPanelStateInternal` / `this.rightPanelStateInternal`.
- In `initializePenetrator`, drop the `usingInternalState` diagnostic keys from the `console.debug`
  payload — the dual-source condition they reported no longer exists. Keep the rest of the debug object.
- Leave `calculatePositions`, `canSwapRoles`, `canSelectPenetrator`, `togglePenetrator`, the overlay/
  opacity/height getters, `onClose`, `onBackdropClick`, and `resetPositions` otherwise unchanged. In
  particular do not touch the `POSITION_BUFFER = 40` constant or the transform-origin math inside
  `calculatePositions` — per `.claude/skills/attachment-system/SKILL.md` the attachment-point
  coordinates it consumes are in ORIGINAL image pixel space and that must not change.

Template (`penetration-modal.component.html`): `isOpen` is now a signal, so its two template reads
become calls — `[class.open]="isOpen()"` on line 1 and `@if (isOpen())` on line 2. `showContent`
remains a plain field and its reads at lines 37 and 107 are unchanged.

Parent binding (`src/app/app.component.html`): on the `<app-penetration-modal>` element only, delete the
`[leftPanelState]="leftPanelState$ | async"` and `[rightPanelState]="rightPanelState$ | async"` lines
(currently lines 142-143), leaving `[isOpen]="showPenetrationModal"` and
`(close)="showPenetrationModal = false"`. Do NOT touch the two identically-named bindings on
`<app-compare-modal>` a few lines above — that component still declares those inputs.
  </action>

  <action>
Expand `penetration-modal.component.spec.ts` from its single construction test to cover RACE-01's
observable behavior. Keep the existing `TestBed.configureTestingModule({ imports: [PenetrationModalComponent] })`
setup and the `should create` test.

Because `isOpen` is now a signal input, the spec MUST set it with
`fixture.componentRef.setInput('isOpen', true)` followed by `fixture.detectChanges()` — direct
assignment to `component.isOpen` will not compile (D-13).

Add these tests:
1. `shows content immediately when isOpen becomes true` — set the input to `true`, run change
   detection, and assert `component.showContent` is `true` with NO timer advance. Do not wrap this in
   `fakeAsync`/`tick` — needing a tick would mean the deferral survived.
2. `clears content and internal state when isOpen becomes false` — open, then set the input to `false`,
   and assert `component.showContent` is `false` and that `getPenetratorState()` returns `null`.
3. `follows state changes made while open` (D-11) — with the modal open, push a new state through the
   real `StateManagementService` (e.g. `updateLeftPanelModel(...)` with a model fixture) and assert the
   component's `getPenetratorState()`/`getReceiverState()` reflect the new value. Use the real
   root-provided service rather than a mock so the immutable-spread emission path under test is genuine.
4. `does not re-run calculatePositions for an equivalent state emission` — spy on
   `component.calculatePositions`, push the SAME logical state twice, and assert the spy call count
   increments only once (proves the custom `distinctUntilChanged` comparator is doing real work rather
   than being defeated by reference inequality).
5. `stops responding to state emissions after destroy` — open the modal, spy on
   `component.calculatePositions`, call `fixture.destroy()`, push another state change, and assert the
   spy call count did not increase.
6. `does not declare leftPanelState / rightPanelState inputs` — assert
   `'leftPanelState' in component` is `false` and `'rightPanelState' in component` is `false` (D-12's
   structural guarantee, enforced from the spec side).

Where a `PanelState` fixture is needed, copy the complete literal shape used in
`compare-modal.component.spec.ts` (selectedModel, overlays, overlayScales, overlayRotations, scale,
showOverlays, position, horizontalFlip) so the object satisfies the current interface.
  </action>
